unique_paths_iii.brute:
empties = all cells with 0; start = the cell with 1, end = the cell with 2
count = 0
for each ordering of empties:   (k! orderings, each checked only when complete)
    chain = start, then the ordering, then end
    if every consecutive pair in chain shares an edge: count += 1
return count
unique_paths_iii.optimal:
todo = number of empty cells + 1   (the end cell itself must be stepped on too)
find the start cell (start_row, start_col)
count_walks(row, col, todo):
    if grid[row][col] == 2: return 1 if todo == 0 else 0
    saved = grid[row][col], grid[row][col] = -1   (mark: on the path right now)
    count = 0
    for each of the 4 neighbours (next_row, next_col):
        if in bounds and grid[next_row][next_col] is 0 or 2: count += count_walks(next_row, next_col, todo - 1)
    grid[row][col] = saved
    return count
return count_walks(start_row, start_col, todo)

n_queens.optimal:
result = empty list
place(row, queens, cols, diag, anti):
    if row == n: append the board drawn from queens to result, return
    for each column col:
        if col in cols or row - col in diag or row + col in anti: skip   (under attack: whole subtree pruned)
        add col to cols, row - col to diag, row + col to anti; push col on queens
        place(row + 1, queens, cols, diag, anti)
        pop queens; remove col, row - col, row + col from the sets
place(0, [], {}, {}, {})
return result

sudoku_solver.optimal:
rows, cols, boxes = 9 bitmasks each of the digits already used; empties = list of empty cells
for each filled cell: set its digit's bit in its row, column and box mask
candidates(row, col) = digits 1..9 whose bit is off in rows[row] | cols[col] | box mask
fill():
    if empties is empty: return true
    i = index of the empty cell with the fewest candidates; remove it from empties   (most constrained first)
    for each digit from 1 to 9 whose bit is in candidates(row, col):
        set the bit in rows[row], cols[col], boxes[box]; board[row][col] = digit
        if fill(): return true
        clear the bit in rows[row], cols[col], boxes[box]
    board[row][col] = empty; put the cell back at index i of empties
    return false
fill()

remove_invalid_parentheses.brute:
kept = empty set
for each mask from 0 to 2^n - 1:   (bit i on = keep s[i])
    candidate = the characters s[i] whose bit is on
    if candidate is valid (balance never drops below 0 and ends at 0): add candidate to kept
longest = max length in kept
return every string in kept with length == longest

expression_add_operators.optimal:
result = empty list
extend(i, expr, value, last):   (last = the most recent multiplicative term, with its sign)
    if i == n: if value == target: append expr to result; return
    for each j from i + 1 to n:
        piece = num[i..j)
        if piece has a leading zero and length > 1: stop
        current = piece as an integer
        if i == 0: extend(j, piece, current, current)
        else:
            extend(j, expr + "+" + piece, value + current, current)
            extend(j, expr + "-" + piece, value - current, -current)
            extend(j, expr + "*" + piece, value - last + last * current, last * current)   (undo last, re-add the product)
extend(0, "", 0, 0)
return result

robot_room_cleaner.brute:
visited = empty set, heading = 0
face(wanted): turn right until heading == wanted
walk(path, forward): replay the recorded moves from the start, or their reverses from the end
explore(row, col, path):
    add (row, col) to visited, clean
    for each direction:
        if the neighbour in that direction is not visited:
            face(direction)
            if move succeeds:
                explore(neighbour, path + [direction])
                walk back to the start along path + [direction], then walk forward along path   (return via the origin)
explore(0, 0, [])
robot_room_cleaner.optimal:
visited = empty set of cells, directions in clockwise order
go_back: turn around (two rights), move one step, turn around again   (undo one move, keep the heading)
clean_from(row, col, heading):
    add (row, col) to visited, clean
    for each k in 0..3:
        direction = (heading + k) mod 4, (next_row, next_col) = neighbour in that direction
        if (next_row, next_col) not visited and move succeeds:
            clean_from(next_row, next_col, direction)
            go_back
        turn right
clean_from(0, 0, 0)

minimum_number_of_taps_to_open_to_water_.optimal:
reach = array of n + 1 zeros   (reach[left] = furthest right end of any tap starting at left)
for each tap i:
    left = max(0, i - ranges[i])
    reach[left] = max(reach[left], i + ranges[i])
taps = 0, current_end = 0, farthest = 0
for each position i from 0 to n - 1:
    farthest = max(farthest, reach[i])
    if i == current_end:   (edge of the wet prefix: one more tap is needed, like Jump Game II)
        if farthest <= i: return -1
        taps = taps + 1
        current_end = farthest
return taps

min_number_operations.brute:
current = array of n zeros, operations = 0
repeat forever:
    i = 0
    while i < n and current[i] >= target[i]: i = i + 1
    if i == n: return operations
    while i < n and current[i] < target[i]:   (one stroke: add 1 across the whole needy run)
        current[i] = current[i] + 1
        i = i + 1
    operations = operations + 1

super_washing_machines.brute:
if total % n != 0: return -1
goal = tuple of n copies of total / n
distance = dict state -> moves, distance[start] = 0
queue of states = [start]   (BFS, one move = every machine passes 0 or 1 dress)
while the queue is not empty:
    current = pop from the front
    if current == goal: return distance[current]
    for each choice of direction (-1, 0, +1) per machine:
        next = current after each machine passes one dress in its direction (invalid if an empty machine passes)
        if next is valid and not in distance:
            distance[next] = distance[current] + 1
            append next to the queue
return -1
super_washing_machines.optimal:
total = sum of machines, n = number of machines
if total % n != 0: return -1
target = total / n
best = 0, balance = 0   (balance = net dresses that must cross the boundary to the right of here)
for each load in machines:
    excess = load - target
    balance = balance + excess
    best = max(best, |balance|, excess)   (one dress crosses a boundary per move; a machine gives one per move)
return best

patching_array.brute:
arr = copy of nums, patches = 0
repeat forever:
    sums = set of every subset sum of arr that is <= n   (add each x to every sum found so far)
    missing = smallest value in 1..n not in sums
    if nothing is missing: return patches
    append missing to arr
    patches = patches + 1

set_intersection_size_at_least_two.optimal:
order = (end, -start) for each interval, sorted   (end ascending, ties by start descending)
a = b = -1   (the two largest chosen points so far, a < b)
count = 0
for each (end, start) in order:
    if start > b:   (neither chosen point is inside: take the two rightmost points)
        a = end - 1, b = end
        count = count + 2
    else if start > a:   (only b is inside: add end)
        a = b, b = end
        count = count + 1
return count

couples_holding_hands.brute:
start = the row as a tuple
distance = dict seating -> swaps, distance[start] = 0
queue of seatings = [start]   (BFS over seatings)
while the queue is not empty:
    current = pop from the front
    if every couch (2i, 2i + 1) holds a couple: return distance[current]
    for each pair of seats i < j:
        swapped = current with seats i and j exchanged
        if swapped not in distance:
            distance[swapped] = distance[current] + 1
            append swapped to the queue
return -1

stamping_the_sequence.brute:
start = string of n '?'
previous = dict string -> (string before it, stamp position), previous[start] = none
queue of strings = [start]   (BFS over stampings)
while the queue is not empty:
    current = pop from the front
    if current == target: follow previous back to start collecting positions, return them in forward order
    for each position i from 0 to n - m:
        stamped = current with the stamp written at i
        if stamped not in previous:
            previous[stamped] = (current, i)
            append stamped to the queue
return []
stamping_the_sequence.optimal:
letters = target as a list, done = array of n - m + 1 false values
moves = [], erased_total = 0   (work backwards: erase stamps into '?')
while erased_total < n:
    progressed = false
    for each position i from 0 to n - m:
        if done[i]: skip
        erased = unstamp(i): if every real letter in window i matches the stamp, turn them into '?' and count them, else 0
        if erased > 0:   (this window was the last stamp laid here)
            erased_total = erased_total + erased
            append i to moves, done[i] = true, progressed = true
    if not progressed: return []
return moves reversed
